notes: Sensor suite is 2x grayscale stereo + 2x color stereo cameras (4 total), 1x Velodyne HDL-64E LiDAR, and 1x OXTS RT3003 GPS/IMU INS; no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras on the original platform.

Recorded in Karlsruhe, Germany using a VW station wagon with 2 color + 2 grayscale stereo camera pairs, Velodyne HDL-64E LiDAR, and a combined GPS/IMU (OXTS RT3003); no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors; download requires free registration on the official site.
Tracking benchmark is a sub-task of the broader KITTI suite; downloads include left/right stereo images, Velodyne LiDAR point clouds, and GPS/IMU data, all requiring free user registration.

A 579-image subset of the KITTI raw dataset (Fritsch et al., ITSC 2013) recorded in Karlsruhe, Germany; the base kit provides left color images, calibration, and labels, while LiDAR/GPS/IMU data come from the underlying KITTI raw sequences requiring separate download with free registration.
Ground truth for stereo/flow/scene flow is derived from a Velodyne HDL-64E LiDAR and OXTS RT 3003 GPS/IMU; download requires free account registration at cvlibs.net.
Built on KITTI Raw Data; inherits all raw sensors (stereo color+grayscale cameras, Velodyne HDL-64 LiDAR, RTK GPS/IMU); benchmark submission and test-set download require KITTI account registration.

Sensors confirmed from the official IJRR paper (Geiger et al., 2013): 2 grayscale stereo + 2 color stereo cameras, Velodyne HDL-64E LiDAR, and OXTS RT3003 GPS/IMU; no radar, fisheye, event, or CAN bus data included; download requires free registration.
KITTI-360 includes stereo perspective cameras, fisheye cameras, Velodyne HDL-64 + SICK LiDAR, and GPS/IMU (OXTS); no radar, event, or thermal cameras documented; download requires free registration.

SemanticKITTI adds dense LiDAR semantic labels atop the KITTI Odometry Benchmark; the underlying KITTI raw data (stereo cameras, Velodyne HDL-64E, OXTS GPS/IMU) requires free registration at cvlibs.net, while SemanticKITTI labels are directly downloadable from semantic-kitti.org.

Fully synthetic dataset (CARLA v0.9.10) mirroring the KITTI sensor rig (Velodyne HDL64 + two colour cameras); provides semantic labels, depth images, and odometry poses but no IMU/GPS/radar as CARLA simulation does not replicate those KITTI sensors.

Purely synthetic dataset (Unity engine) providing only monocular RGB images plus ground-truth depth, optical flow, and segmentation; no physical sensors (LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS) are simulated, and Virtual KITTI 2 explicitly lists LiDAR as a future addition.
Fully synthetic dataset rendered in Unity; provides RGB, depth, segmentation, optical/scene flow, and stereo images — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS modalities exist as it is not real-world collected.
Depth is derived from stereo disparity (no LiDAR); metadata includes GPS, vehicle odometry, and outside temperature; IMU is not explicitly documented.

Cityscapes 3D extends the base Cityscapes dataset (stereo video, GPS, vehicle odometry) with 9-DoF 3D bounding box annotations for vehicles; access requires free registration at cityscapes-dataset.com; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, fisheye, or event camera present.

Foggy Cityscapes is a purely image-based synthetic dataset created by simulating fog on real Cityscapes stereo RGB frames using depth maps; it inherits Cityscapes' stereo imagery but adds no new sensor modalities, and download requires a free Cityscapes account registration.

RainCityscapes is a synthetic rain-removal dataset built from Cityscapes real photos with algorithmically added rain streaks and fog; hosted on the Cityscapes website requiring free registration to download.

Image-only dataset of 101 real foggy road scenes from Zurich; no sensor modalities beyond monocular camera images are present; introduced alongside the SFSU paper (arXiv:1708.07819, IJCV 2018) by Sakaridis, Dai & Van Gool.
3808 real foggy images captured on Zurich streets; only monocular camera images with sparse semantic annotations for 16–40 dense-fog frames; no other sensor modalities documented.
Image-only dataset with 35,000 unlabeled and 50 densely labeled real nighttime/dusk driving frames; no non-camera sensors documented.

Sensors explicitly documented are: one frame (monocular) camera, LiDAR, radar, event camera, and a combined IMU/GNSS unit; no stereo, fisheye, thermal, CAN bus, or explicit ego-pose trajectory data are mentioned in the paper or SDK.

WildDash 1 is a purely image-based benchmark (monocular frames sourced from dashcam/internet videos) for semantic and instance segmentation; no range, inertial, or odometry sensors are included. Free download requires account registration at wilddash.cc.
WildDash 2 is a camera-only (monocular RGB images) panoptic/semantic segmentation benchmark with 4,256+ real-world driving frames; no ranging, inertial, or vehicle bus sensors are included.

nuImages is a camera-only 2D image dataset (93k annotated frames) spun off from nuScenes; the schema explicitly states sensor modality is 'always camera', and ego_pose is included but no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or CAN bus data are distributed with it.

nuScenes-LidarSeg is an extension of the base nuScenes dataset (same sensor suite: 6 monocular cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 RADARs, GPS/IMU, CAN bus, ego poses), adding per-point semantic labels for 32 classes across 1.4 billion annotated LiDAR points; free for academic use but requires registration at nuscenes.org.

Panoptic nuScenes is a direct extension of the original nuScenes dataset (6 surround monocular cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 radars, GPS, IMU, CAN bus), adding point-wise panoptic segmentation and tracking labels; data was collected in Boston and Singapore and requires free registration at nuscenes.org to download.

Sensor suite confirmed as 5 LiDARs, 8 monocular cameras, GNSS & IMU across 31 vehicles; no radar or CAN bus expansion (that feature belongs to nuScenes); download requires free account registration and Terms of Use agreement.

nuScenes-QA is a VQA benchmark (460K QA pairs, AAAI 2024) built on top of the real-world nuScenes sensor dataset; QA annotations are freely available on GitHub, but the underlying nuScenes raw sensor data requires registration at nuscenes.org.

nuScenes-MQA is a caption and QA annotation layer on top of the base nuScenes dataset (real-world, Boston/Singapore); sensor data inherits nuScenes' full suite (6 monocular cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 radars, GPS, IMU, CAN bus, ego pose), while the MQA annotations themselves are freely available on GitHub.

nuPrompt is a language-prompt annotation layer built directly on top of the real-world nuScenes dataset (6 cameras, 5 radars, 1 lidar, IMU, GPS, CAN bus); it adds 40,147 natural-language descriptions of object tracklets and does not introduce new sensor modalities beyond what nuScenes provides.

Talk2Car is a natural-language object referral dataset built directly on top of nuScenes; all nuScenes sensor modalities (6 monocular cameras for 360° coverage, LiDAR, 5 RADARs, IMU, GPS, CAN bus, ego pose) are accessible, but require downloading the full 300 GB+ nuScenes release separately.

Occ3D-nuScenes is a 3D occupancy prediction benchmark derived from the real-world nuScenes dataset (6 surround cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 radars, GPS, IMU, CAN bus, ego pose); access requires agreeing to nuScenes terms of use via registration.

Occ3D-Waymo is a 3D occupancy prediction benchmark derived from the Waymo Open Dataset (5 monocular cameras + LiDAR); accessing the base data requires free registration at waymo.com/open/licensing, while occupancy labels are released on GitHub.
OpenScene is a compact redistribution of nuPlan (5 LiDARs, 8 surround cameras, GNSS/IMU); no radar present; download requires nuPlan registration via OpenXLab/nuplan.org.

UniOcc is a unified benchmark (not a raw-sensor dataset) that aggregates occupancy labels, camera images, LiDAR-derived voxel annotations, and per-voxel flow from nuScenes & Waymo (real) and CARLA & OpenCOOD (synthetic); raw IMU/GPS/CAN signals are not explicitly exposed by UniOcc itself.
The Perception dataset releases 5 cameras and 5 LiDARs with ego pose/IMU/GNSS; radar is part of Waymo's production vehicle suite but is NOT included in the released Perception dataset files.

WOMD primarily provides processed agent trajectories + HD maps; LiDAR point clouds were added in v1.2 (2023) via WOMD-LiDAR, and only camera embeddings (not raw images) were added in v1.2.1 (2024); no raw IMU/GPS/radar/camera streams are distributed.

WOMD-Reasoning is a language Q&A annotation layer (3M pairs) built on top of the real-world Waymo Open Motion Dataset; it does not independently include raw sensor streams (camera/LiDAR/radar/IMU/GPS), though its vision extension references WOMD camera patches, and ego-pose/trajectory data is inherited from the underlying WOMD scenarios; access requires Waymo registration and terms acceptance.

WOD-E2E is explicitly a vision-based benchmark using 8 synchronized camera streams and ego states/trajectories; LiDAR and radar are not part of this E2E sub-dataset, though they exist in other Waymo Open Dataset splits.

Sensors include 2 LiDAR, 7 ring cameras (monocular 360°), and 2 front-facing stereo cameras; 6-DOF ego pose provided via GPS+sensor-based localization; no radar, fisheye, thermal, or event cameras documented; raw IMU/CAN bus data not explicitly included in the public release.

The Motion Forecasting split contains only 2D bird's-eye-view object trajectories and HD map data (no raw sensor streams); raw sensors such as cameras and LiDAR are exclusive to the Argoverse 1 3D Tracking dataset.
Radar is explicitly absent (the paper contrasts AV2 stereo imagery against nuScenes radar); ego-pose is provided as city_SE3_egovehicle transforms but raw IMU/GPS/CAN data are not released.

The AV2 LiDAR Dataset is LiDAR-only (20,000 unlabeled sequences); it explicitly excludes imagery, annotations, radar, and raw IMU/GNSS — only lidar sweeps, HD maps, and map-aligned 6-DOF ego-vehicle pose are released.

The Motion Forecasting subset distributes only actor trajectory tracks, HD maps, and ego-vehicle pose — no raw sensor streams (camera, lidar, radar, IMU, GPS) are included; those reside exclusively in the separate AV2 Sensor and Lidar datasets.
TbV shares the AV2 sensor rig (7 ring cameras, 2 stereo cameras, dual 32-beam LiDAR, 6-DOF ego-pose); raw IMU/GPS/CAN channels are not explicitly documented in any official TbV page.
Argoverse-HD uses only the center ring camera from Argoverse 1.1 with dense 2D annotations at 30 FPS; LiDAR and other sensors from Argoverse 1.1 are explicitly excluded from this dataset.

The Prediction Dataset (2020) distributes processed perception outputs (agent tracks, ego poses, semantic maps, traffic lights) in zarr format — not raw sensor streams; radar was used during collection but is not explicitly released in the prediction dataset.

LiDAR, radar, stereo, and fisheye were explicitly noted as future work in the original BAIR blog post; the dataset is camera-only (monocular dashcam) with cell-phone GPS/IMU for trajectory; CAN bus data is not documented.

BDD-X is an annotation layer (natural-language action descriptions and textual explanations) on top of BDD100K dashboard-camera videos; it is camera-only with no additional sensor modalities, and videos require registration via the Berkeley DeepDrive portal.

BDD-OIA is an image-only annotation extension of BDD100K (CVPR 2020), providing 4 action labels and 21 explanation labels on monocular dashcam frames; no raw sensor streams (LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS) are included in the released dataset.

BDD-A is a driver attention/gaze dataset using in-lab eye-tracking over dashcam videos from BDD100K braking events; sensors are limited to a monocular camera and eye tracker — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or CAN bus data are included.
Sensor suite confirmed as 2 LiDARs, 6 monocular video cameras, stereo pairs, and a combined IMU/GNSS system; no radar, fisheye, event, thermal, or CAN bus data found in official documentation.
Lane segmentation sub-dataset uses stereo camera pairs (Camera 5 & 6) from the broader ApolloScape platform; full data download requires emailing the team for access.

Sample data is freely downloadable via wget; full data requires emailing the team. The dataset FAQ explicitly states ego-vehicle trajectory is NOT included; only surrounding agent trajectories are provided.

ApolloCar3D is a 3D car instance sub-dataset of ApolloScape; stereo images and GPS/IMU localization are inherited from the ApolloScape collection platform, but full data access requires emailing the authors rather than direct free download.

Collected in Beijing with 2x Riegl VMX-1HA LiDARs, up to 6 video cameras (incl. stereo pairs), and a combined IMU/GNSS system; full data download requires an email request (academic use only); no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented.

Purely image-based synthetic dataset (10,500 monocular RGB frames, Unity 3D engine) released alongside Gen-LaneNet (ECCV 2020); only 3D lane labels and camera pitch are provided — no additional sensors.

Six cameras (3 wide-angle + 3 fisheye), 5 LiDARs, and CAN/bus signals (GPS, acceleration, angular velocity, steering) recorded on an Audi Q7 e-tron; no radar, stereo, thermal, or event cameras; released under CC BY-ND 4.0 with no registration required.
Access requires emailing opendataset@zenseact.com for approval; radar data was added after the initial release and is only available in Sequences and Drives subsets, not Frames.
GPS/localization data explicitly withheld due to local regulations; vehicle pose transformation matrix is provided; seven monocular cameras + one 40-beam LiDAR; no radar or IMU included.

ONCE-3DLanes is a 3D lane annotation layer built on the ONCE base dataset (NeurIPS 2021); LiDAR is used only for annotation pipeline (label generation), not as a released sensor stream; IMU/GPS/ego-pose presence inherits from the ONCE base dataset but is not explicitly documented in ONCE-3DLanes-specific materials.

H3D is a LiDAR-only dataset (Velodyne HDL-64E); no camera images are released — the data package contains only point clouds, GPS+IMU, CAN bus signals, and 3D labels; access requires a university affiliation and a signed Data Sharing Agreement.

Access requires university affiliation and email registration; dataset contains 104 hours of real driving in SF Bay Area with three cameras (Point Grey Grasshopper), Velodyne LiDAR, GPS traces, and CAN bus signals; IMU presence is not explicitly confirmed in primary documentation.

HAD (HRI Advice Dataset) is built on top of the HDD naturalistic driving dataset and focuses on driving video paired with natural language advice; access requires a signed Data Sharing Agreement and university affiliation (CVPR 2019).
Captured in Tokyo with a GoPro Hero 7; only camera and GoPro IMU (accel+gyro) data are provided; access requires a university affiliation request via the Honda Research Institute USA page.

Collected in Tokyo via instrumented Honda SHUTTLE; dataset includes monocular camera images, 360° LiDAR pointclouds, and odometry (pos/roll/pitch/yaw); no explicit documentation of IMU/GPS/radar/CAN bus; access requires a request/registration for non-commercial use.
Camera-only dataset (SEKONIX SF332X-10X, 30Hz) with optical flow images and natural language risk annotations; access restricted to university researchers via Honda HRI request form.
Dataset uses 3 Point Grey Grasshopper cameras, Velodyne HDL-64E S2 LiDAR, high-precision GPS, and CAN bus data; IMU/INS and ego-pose trajectory not explicitly confirmed in available documentation.
Radar is only available in the separate Oxford Radar RobotCar Dataset extension (2019); the base dataset does not include it. Registration requires an academic email address.

Requires registration with an academic email and a Google account for authorized Google Drive download; inherits all original RobotCar sensors (3 stereo + 3 mono cameras, 2D/3D LiDARs, GPS/INS, CAN bus) and adds a Navtech CTS350-X FMCW radar with ground-truth radar odometry.

This is a camera-image annotation dataset (left/right stereo lenses) derived from the Oxford RobotCar Dataset, focused solely on road-boundary masks; it does not redistribute raw LiDAR, IMU, GPS, radar, or other sensor streams from the parent dataset.

Primary released data is millimetre-wave scanning radar + GPS/INS (GNSS + IMU); LiDAR is used internally for reference motion generation but its release as a data stream is not explicitly confirmed in the paper abstract or project page.

RobotCar Seasons is a curated subset of the Oxford RobotCar dataset used as a visual localization benchmark; ground truth poses are derived from LiDAR+SfM alignment (not raw GPS/INS) and the dataset/evaluation server is hosted at visuallocalization.net.

Dataset provides only undistorted images from two front-facing (non-stereo, oblique-mounted) monocular cameras and 6-DOF ground-truth poses; raw sensor streams (GPS, IMU, LiDAR) were used only for GT construction and are not distributed.

Image-only visual localization benchmark (6-DOF poses provided for reference/DB images, withheld for queries); GPS/INS were used during collection but are not distributed; licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and freely downloadable without registration.

This dataset provides 2D-2D cross-season image correspondences derived from the CMU Seasons and RobotCar Seasons datasets; LiDAR was used internally to generate correspondences but raw LiDAR data is not distributed, and GPS/INS was used to initialize camera poses for the reference traversal.
Sensor suite is stereo camera + IMU + RTK-GNSS only; no LiDAR or radar; ego poses derived from VIO fused with RTK-GNSS.

MulRan is a range-sensor-focused dataset (Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR + Navtech CTS350-X radar) with no camera modality; IMU and GPS were officially added in November 2020 and 6D baseline trajectories are provided as ground truth.

Cameras are a Point Grey Ladybug3 omnidirectional (fisheye-based multi-lens) unit; no monocular/stereo/thermal/radar sensors present; wheel odometry serves as CAN-bus-equivalent proprioceptive odometry; KVH Fiber Optic Gyro supplements the Microstrain IMU; ground-truth pose from SLAM graph is provided.

dataset_name: Ford Campus Vision and LiDAR Dataset
notes: Camera is a Point Grey Ladybug3 omnidirectional (spherical multi-lens) system, not a standard monocular/stereo/fisheye; two Riegl push-broom LiDARs and one Velodyne HDL-64E are included; ego-pose provided by Applanix POS LV GPS/INS.

Each vehicle carries an Applanix POS-LV GNSS/INS, 4× HDL-32E Velodyne LiDARs, 2 stereo pairs + 2 side monocular 1.3 MP cameras + 1 forward 5 MP dash camera (7 total); no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented, and CAN bus data is not explicitly included in the released Rosbags.

Dataset includes one stereo camera (Bumblebee2, 20 fps), five laser scanners, an Xsens MTi IMU, and a low-cost GPS; no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras, and no CAN bus or ego-pose ground truth are documented.

Sensor suite includes stereo camera (PointGrey Flea3), 2D SICK and 3D Velodyne LiDARs, Xsens IMU, Fiber Optic Gyro (FOG), wheel encoder, commercial GPS, and VRS-GPS; no radar, fisheye, thermal, or event camera present.
Sensors explicitly confirmed: co-aligned RGB+Thermal monocular, RGB stereo, Velodyne VLP-32E LiDAR, GPS/IMU; no radar or CAN bus mentioned in any official source.
Hardware consists solely of a color camera and thermal camera joined by a beam splitter; no LiDAR, GPS, IMU, or radar — those sensors appear only in the separate KAIST All-Day (T-ITS 2018) dataset.

Radar (FMCW mmWave AWR1642) is only present in the Winter Extension; base dataset has 4 RGB cameras (frontal stereo + 2 lateral), 2 Velodyne LiDARs, IR/thermal camera, IMU, and RTK GNSS; data distributed freely via torrent under MIT license.

Dataset includes 4 RGB cameras, 1 IR/thermal camera, 3× 3D LiDARs, FMCW radar (winter-only), RTK GNSS, and IMU; stereo configuration is mentioned in the original BUD but not explicitly confirmed for the Winter Extension; data distributed freely via torrent.
SF sequences use 6 monocular cameras (360° rig); HK sequences add a fisheye sky camera; integrated GNSS/INS via NovAtel SPAN-CPT provides ego-pose; no radar or stereo camera documented.

Dataset focuses on GNSS positioning in urban canyons (Hong Kong & Tokyo); sensors include monocular camera, mechanical and solid-state LiDARs, multiple IMUs (commercial + tactical grade), and GNSS receivers; ground truth from SPAN-CPT; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras found in any official documentation.

Dataset uses 8 monocular Ximea MQ013CG-E2 cameras (no stereo/fisheye/radar), Velodyne VLP-32C LiDAR, Novatel OEM638 GNSS+INS, Xsens IMUs, and a Dataspeed ADAS CAN-bus kit; available under a Scale AI/UWaterloo Terms of Use requiring acceptance before download.

Sensor suite is a single 5MP FLIR Blackfly S monocular camera, 128-beam Velodyne Alpha-Prime LiDAR, 360° Navtech radar, and Applanix POS LV GNSS-INS (with wheel encoder); no stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras; data freely accessible via AWS S3 Open Data Registry without registration.

Four monocular cameras and LiDAR confirmed; GPS/INS explicitly stated for cross-route correspondence; no radar, stereo, fisheye, or event camera evidence found; IMU and CAN bus not explicitly documented.

Publicly released portion is LiDAR-only (semanticKITTI format); full 26 TB multi-modal data (cameras, radar, GNSS/IMU) documented in SPIE papers but only labeled LiDAR sequences are downloadable from the project page.

Confirmed sensors are stereo RGB camera, active gated NIR camera, FIR (thermal) camera, Velodyne LiDAR, and radar; GPS/IMU/odometry presence on the research platform is likely but not explicitly documented in publicly available sources.

Registration via web form required to receive Dropbox download link; dataset is non-commercial/academic only (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); GPS and IMU are stored together in a combined file providing latitude/longitude/altitude plus full IMU orientation, angular velocity, and linear acceleration; no explicit CAN bus or standalone ego-pose trajectory files documented.
Raincouver (IEEE RA-L 2017) is a monocular camera-only scene parsing benchmark for rainy/night driving; no LiDAR, radar, or other sensors are documented, and no public download portal was found.
Image-only dataset (~1,000 real traffic images collected via Google/Bing web searches); no physical sensor suite — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or vehicle bus data of any kind.

RaidaR is a purely image-based dataset of 58,542 real rainy street scene photos with semantic/instance segmentation labels; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or other non-camera sensor modalities are included.
Fully synthetic dataset built in CARLA; sensor suite covers multi-view monocular RGB, stereo RGB, LiDAR, and depth maps, but no real-world IMU/GPS/radar/fisheye/event/thermal modalities exist.

Camera-only image segmentation dataset for rainy driving scenes; no dedicated public download portal found — data appears shared via Baidu Cloud or upon request through the authors' GitHub (kuijiang94/FMRNet).
Camera-only dataset (single industry-standard RGB camera); no non-visual sensors documented anywhere in the paper or project page.

The dataset's primary sensor is a gated NIR flood-illuminated camera (3 slices per frame); LiDAR provides sparse ground-truth depth; the dataset contains both real-world driving data (~4,000 km, northern Europe) and synthetic data (GTAV-simulated), hosted freely on the Uni Ulm DENSE cloudstore.

The dataset captures real gated-camera slices (monocular, NIR, active illumination) over 4,000 km in Northern Europe; filtered LiDAR point clouds are included for evaluation, but no radar, IMU, GPS, or CAN bus data are documented.

Camera-only semantic segmentation dataset (~174K paired clear/adverse-weather images); data access was tied to CVPR 2024 UG2+ Challenge registration and no unconditional free download link was documented.

This is a physics-based LiDAR snowfall simulation tool (CVPR 2022), not a collected dataset; it augments real clear-weather LiDAR point clouds (from the SeeingThroughFog/STF dataset) with synthetic snow and wet-ground effects, providing only LiDAR data under a non-commercial Creative Commons license.

Dataset (35K frames, 58 sequences) includes 4D radar tensors, dual high-res LiDARs (128-ch + 64-ch), four surround stereo RGB cameras, RTK-GPS, and two IMUs; published under CC BY-NC-ND license and accessible via the KAIST AVELab GitHub with a contact email required for HDD shipping of large sequences.

Stereo camera images can also be used monocularly; ego odometry is a fused output of RTK GPS, IMU, and wheel odometry (~30–100 Hz); access requires institutional affiliation validation before a password-protected download link is issued.

Due to policy restrictions, only the 4D radar point cloud data is publicly released; camera and LiDAR data are withheld; sensors are 4D radar, LiDAR, monocular camera, and GNSS per the ITSC 2022 paper (arXiv:2204.13483); no IMU, CAN bus, or ego-pose trajectory data documented.

Originally hosted at www.astyx.net, the dataset became unavailable after Astyx GmbH was acquired by Cruise (GM); the 546-frame public release contained only radar (Astyx 6455 HiRes 4D), LiDAR (Velodyne VLP-16), and a single front monocular camera (Point Grey Blackfly) with no GPS, IMU, or CAN bus data.

CVPR 2022 dataset by Valeo AI featuring a high-definition radar, monocular camera, LiDAR, GPS, and CAN bus traces; download requires registration via an external link and has experienced storage availability issues.

Dataset releases four automotive radar sensors and a documentary monocular camera; LiDAR was used only for annotation purposes and is not part of the released data; ego-motion-compensated velocities and global/local coordinate positions are provided per detection, but raw GPS/IMU/CAN streams are not explicitly released.

CARRADA contains only synchronized monocular camera and TI AWR1843 short-range radar (range-angle-Doppler) data with no LiDAR, IMU, GPS, or other sensors; annotations were generated semi-automatically using camera information alone.

RADDet uses a TI AWR1843BOOST FMCW radar and a stereo camera only; data was captured from a stationary tripod on sidewalks (not a moving vehicle), so no ego-motion, GPS, IMU, or CAN bus data are present; dataset (10,158 annotated frames) is freely available via Google Drive.
Sensor suite is explicitly a pair of stereo cameras and two 77GHz FMCW radar arrays only; dataset is restricted to academic/non-profit noncommercial use and requires a license agreement for download.

Sensors are TI IWR1443BOOST 77GHz FMCW radar + Intel RealSense D435i (RGB + active-stereo depth + IMU); dataset is freely available on the Illinois Data Bank under CC BY 4.0 with an SDK at github.com/moodoki/radical_sdk.

Sensors explicitly documented: FLIR stereo cameras, Ouster OS-1 LiDAR, Oculii Eagle 4D radar, Xsens MTi630 IMU, RTK-GPS (Synerex MRP-2000) and GPS (Ublox ZEDF9P), and wheel encoders; dataset is freely downloadable (password: mscrad4r) from the project page or Google Drive.

Dataset collected on NTU Singapore campus using a handcart and unmanned vehicle; explicitly includes all 6 sensors (4D radar, 3D LiDAR, visual camera, thermal camera, IMU, RTK GPS) with fine-tuned ground-truth odometry for SLAM; no stereo, fisheye, event camera, or CAN bus data.

Sensor rig per platform includes a ZED2i stereo camera, one or two 4D radars (e.g., ARS548, Eagle G7), a 3D LiDAR, one or two IMUs (e.g., MTi-3DK), a GNSS/INS system, and wheel encoders (6M+ frames); reference trajectories generated via LiDAR scan registration to a TLS point cloud map; dataset released under the Open Database License (ODbL), freely downloadable via OneDrive/Baidu Netdisk.

Focuses on heterogeneous radar SLAM (4D phased-array + spinning radar + FMCW LiDAR); stereo camera data was added post-release (March 2025); no evidence of fisheye, event, or thermal cameras, or CAN bus data.

No camera included in the original ColoRadar dataset (the 2025 extension ColoRadar+ adds RGB-D); ground truth poses are derived from lidar SLAM pose graph and Vicon motion capture (one lab sequence), not GPS/GNSS.

Sensors explicitly documented are one high-resolution camera, one 80-line mechanical LiDAR, two 4D radars (Arbe Phoenix and ARS548 RDI), and GPS for timing; no IMU, ego pose, or CAN bus data mentioned in paper or GitHub.

OLIMP uses exactly four sensors: a monocular camera, a UWB short-range radar, a narrow-band long-range radar (ARS 404-21), and a microphone; no LiDAR, stereo, thermal, IMU, or GPS are part of this dataset.
Access requires institutional email validation via GitHub request; core sensors are radar (4D imaging), LiDAR, RGB camera, and ego odometry — IMU/GPS not explicitly documented in available sources.

Dataset includes 2 pinhole cameras (front/back) and 2 fisheye cameras (left/right), 1 spinning LiDAR, 2 radars, and a combined GNSS+INS sensor; full ~85 GB download requires filling a registration form for non-commercial use only.
Explicitly confirmed sensors are cameras, LiDARs (Leddar Pixell flash + rotating), radar, and IMU; GPS/GNSS, ego-pose, and CAN bus presence are not explicitly documented in available public sources.

Pure image-based vehicle detection dataset (5MP monocular camera, freeways); the project page explicitly notes odometry data does not yet exist and invites future requests, confirming no ancillary sensors are present.
USV-based dataset using a 4D radar and monocular camera; published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and freely available at waterscenes.github.io; no LiDAR, stereo, fisheye, thermal, or CAN bus data documented.

Paper (arXiv 2407.12803) confirms 9 imaging radar sensors, 4 cameras (type unspecified), 64-channel LiDAR, and GPS/IMU; dataset public availability and exact camera modalities not confirmed from accessible sources.

Dataset contains only monocular camera and LiDAR modalities; ego pose is provided via virtuallidar-to-world calibration transforms, but no raw GPS/IMU/CAN bus streams are included; download requires registration at thudair.baai.ac.cn.

DAIR-V2X-C is the cooperative subset of DAIR-V2X (CVPR 2022), containing only monocular camera and LiDAR modalities from both vehicle-side and infrastructure-side; dataset download requires registration/application via the official DAIR-V2X portal; ego_pose_trajectory inferred from virtuallidar_to_world calibration files present in the dataset.

DAIR-V2X-I is the infrastructure-only subset of DAIR-V2X (CVPR 2022), containing monocular camera and LiDAR frames from static roadside sensors; no vehicle ego-motion, IMU, GPS, or radar are present; dataset download requires registration at thudair.baai.ac.cn.

DAIR-V2X-V is the vehicle-side-only subset of DAIR-V2X (CVPR 2022); sensors are explicitly documented as one forward-facing monocular RGB camera and a 40-beam LiDAR at 10Hz; dataset download requires registration via thudair.baai.ac.cn and is freely accessible within mainland China.

V2X-Seq (CVPR 2023) extends the DAIR-V2X dataset with sequential tracking/forecasting data; sensors are LiDAR and monocular camera only; full dataset requires registration via the DAIR-V2X portal, though example splits are freely downloadable.

Fully synthetic dataset (CARLA + OpenCDA); each CAV has 4 RGB cameras, 1 LiDAR, GPS/IMU; true and GPS-noisy ego poses stored per-frame in YAML metadata; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented.

OPV2V-H is a synthetic heterogeneous extension of OPV2V (CARLA + OpenCDA), introduced in the ICLR 2024 HEAL paper; agents carry diverse camera and LiDAR configurations, with GPS/IMU inherited from the OPV2V base; no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors are documented.

V2XSet is a fully synthetic dataset generated in CARLA simulator for the V2X-ViT (ECCV 2022) paper; sensors include LiDAR and RGB cameras with simulated GPS noise and ego pose/trajectory, but no physical IMU, radar, or CAN bus.

Fully synthetic dataset built on CARLA; each vehicle has 6 RGB cameras, 1 LiDAR, 1 IMU, and 1 GNSS; roadside units have 4 RGB cameras and 1 LiDAR; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors are present; dataset follows nuScenes schema and is freely downloadable via Google Drive.

Each vehicle carries a Velodyne VLP-32 LiDAR, two monocular cameras (front/rear), and GPS/IMU; no stereo, fisheye, event, thermal, or radar sensors are documented; data is freely downloadable from the UCLA Mobility Lab project page without stated registration.

Each vehicle is equipped with a 128-beam LiDAR, four ZED 2i stereo cameras, and a GPS/IMU integration system; infrastructure units carry 128/64-beam LiDARs and cameras; no radar, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented; dataset is publicly downloadable via the UCLA Mobility Lab project page without registration.

Dataset hosted on HuggingFace (yanglei18/V2X-Radar) requiring account registration; GitHub at yanglei18/V2X-Radar; NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight; multi-view monocular cameras (3 on infrastructure, 1 on vehicle); GPS/IMU used for synchronization and localization; no evidence of stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras.
V2X-R is the first simulated V2X dataset with LiDAR, camera, and 4D radar, generated via CARLA+OpenCDA; IMU/GPS/CAN not documented in any released data files or paper sensor table.
Fully synthetic V2X dataset generated with CARLA simulator providing temporally-aligned RGB images and LiDAR point clouds from vehicles and RSUs; no IMU/GPS/radar sensors documented.
Synthetic CARLA-based dataset with only multi-view RGB cameras and LiDAR documented; ego pose likely present via nuScenes-style format but not explicitly confirmed in public docs.

The A9 Highway releases (R0/R1) explicitly document Basler monocular cameras and Ouster OS1-64 LiDARs; while the broader TUMTraf infrastructure platform includes Doppler radars, event cameras, GPS and IMU, these are not explicitly confirmed for the A9 Highway subset specifically, and as a roadside infrastructure dataset there is no ego-vehicle odometry or pose data.

Infrastructure/roadside-only dataset with two monocular cameras and two LiDARs on intersection gantry bridges; no onboard/ego vehicle sensors; download requires registration at innovation-mobility.com.

CVPR 2024 real-world V2X dataset with 9 sensors (5 roadside + 4 onboard); sensors confirmed are monocular RGB cameras (Basler), Ouster/Velodyne LiDARs, GPS, and IMU; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras documented; dataset is freely available on Zenodo.
Roadside infrastructure dataset pairing only event-based and RGB frame cameras; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS; available via registration at innovationmobility.com.

RoScenes is a vision-only (camera-only) roadside infrastructure dataset; camera extrinsics/intrinsics and UAV-to-World homography are provided for BEV projection, but no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS data are included; dataset is downloadable via ModelScope under a non-commercial license.

LiDAR was used only during data collection for 3D annotation purposes via a LiDAR-equipped vehicle; the released dataset contains only roadside monocular camera images and is geographically restricted to users in China.

HoloVIC (CVPR 2024) explicitly documents only 3 sensor types — monocular camera, fisheye camera, and LiDAR — across 4 intersection layouts; radar, IMU, GPS, and CAN bus are not mentioned in any official source; ego-pose/global trajectories are annotated via cross-device object ID association; public availability via holovic.net likely requires registration per SenseAuto Research policy.

InScope is a real-world infrastructure-side dataset using dual/multi-position LiDARs only (principal + secondary); no camera, radar, or vehicle-ego sensors are documented; public download availability not confirmed from available sources.
Three CAVs equipped with LiDAR (heterogeneous), Microstrain IMU, GNSS, and UWB sensors over a 4 km urban route in Hannover; no camera or radar sensors documented in official sources.

IPS300+ is a roadside infrastructure dataset (not ego-vehicle) using LiDAR and binocular (stereo) cameras mounted at a Beijing intersection; radar, IMU, GPS, and ego-pose are not explicitly documented in available sources.
Purely synthetic (AirSim+CARLA); each UAV carries 5 RGB + 5 semantic cameras only; ego poses available via simulation; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS documented.

CVPR 2024 roadside infrastructure dataset with 50k images and 30k LiDAR point clouds; part of the DAIR family, likely requiring registration via OpenDataLab; no radar, IMU, or GPS modalities documented.

Infrastructure-side (roadside) dataset only — two RGB cameras and a 32-beam LiDAR mounted ~4.5 m high on VANJEE smart base stations; no ego-vehicle, radar, IMU, or GNSS sensors are documented in the paper.
CODD is a CARLA-simulated, LiDAR-only cooperative driving dataset; vehicle pose/trajectory data is included for multi-agent SLAM, but no camera, radar, IMU, or GPS modalities are present.

Fully synthetic dataset (CARLA+SUMO co-simulation); RGB camera and LiDAR are explicitly confirmed; radar is mentioned by a secondary source (aimodels.fyi) but not in the official abstract or GitHub README, so marked unknown; IMU/GNSS/ego-pose not explicitly documented in available sources despite CARLA's capability.

Handheld (not vehicle-mounted) dataset collected at New College Oxford; original release uses Intel RealSense D435i stereo-inertial camera + Ouster OS-1 64 LiDAR with IMU; multi-cam extension adds Sevensense Alphasense with 4 fisheye cameras; 6-DoF ground truth poses derived from scan-to-map registration, no GPS or radar sensors present.

Platform integrates 11 heterogeneous sensors: 2 stereo cameras (Bumblebee XB3/BB2), 2 fisheye/monocular Pixelink cameras, 3 LiDARs (2× Velodyne HDL-32E + ibeo LUX 4L), Continental ARS 308 radar, Xsens IMU, and Magellan ProFlex 500 GNSS-RTK; CAN bus/odometry not explicitly documented in official sources.

HeLiMOS is a LiDAR-only MOS label dataset derived from HeLiPR (which includes IMU/GPS), but HeLiMOS itself only formally documents four heterogeneous LiDAR sensors (OS2-128, Livox Avia, Aeva Aeries II, VLP-16C); IMU/GPS availability from the underlying HeLiPR data is unconfirmed for HeLiMOS specifically.

LIBRE (LiDAR Benchmarking and Reference) features 10 LiDARs plus RGB, IR, 360°, and event cameras, IMU, GNSS, and CAN bus; a 360° camera is included but it is unconfirmed whether it uses a fisheye lens specifically; no radar or stereo camera are mentioned in the paper.

Sensors are explicitly documented: Ouster OS1-128 LiDAR, Carnegie Robotics MultiSense S21 stereo camera (also used for monocular depth benchmarks), and OxTS RT3000v3 GNSS/INS; full dataset requires form-based registration request despite being described as open-access.

SensatUrban is a UAV photogrammetry-based 3D point cloud dataset (~3B points, 3 UK cities) focused on semantic segmentation; it is NOT a sensor-suite driving dataset — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS streams are distributed, only labeled colored point clouds reconstructed from aerial imagery.

Dataset is LiDAR-only (Velodyne HDL-32E); GPS (Novatel FlexPak 6) and IMU (Ixsea LANDINS) were used for trajectory generation but no camera data is distributed; download requires a password provided on the project page (CC-BY-NC-ND-3.0 license).

Collected with Teledyne Optech Maverick MLS (32-line LiDAR + Ladybug 5 panoramic/fisheye camera + GNSS + SLAM); only point cloud labels are released publicly — raw camera images and IMU streams are not distributed; licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

Collected at Peking University campus using a Hesai Pandora module (40-ch LiDAR + 1 forward-facing color camera + 4 wide-angle mono cameras) plus a GPS/IMU system; camera imagery is not released as part of the dataset, only annotated LiDAR point clouds are publicly distributed under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

LiDAR-only dataset (Velodyne HDL-64E) for domain adaptation between SemanticKITTI and SemanticPOSS; introduced alongside the LiDARNet paper (arXiv:2003.01174); no camera, IMU, GPS, or odometry modalities are included.
LiDAR-only dataset (Velodyne HDL-32) collected at Luxembourg Garden, Paris; publicly downloadable with a password shown on the project page; no camera, radar, or CAN bus data documented.

Dataset combines real Paris LiDAR+Ladybug5 (6-camera fisheye) scans with CARLA-simulated equivalents; IMU/GPS/trajectory may be used internally for the mobile mapping system but are not explicitly documented as released dataset modalities.

IDD is a dataset family from IIIT Hyderabad; the base IDD uses a front-facing monocular camera only, while IDD Multimodal adds stereo camera, 16-channel LiDAR, GPS (15 Hz), and 5-parameter CAN/OBD bus data; download requires free registration at insaan.iiit.ac.in.

Dataset uses multiple monocular cameras and LiDAR confirmed; IMU/GPS/ego-pose not explicitly documented in accessible sources; data availability is via project page request (GitHub repo noted 'coming soon' at time of publication).

IDD-X is a camera-only dual-view (front + rear monocular) video dataset focused on important object localization and explanation annotations; no additional sensors (LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS) are mentioned in the paper or project page.

Dataset consists of 5,000 paired RGB and Near-Infrared (NIR) monocular camera images with pixel-level semantic segmentation annotations; no LiDAR, radar, or other sensor modalities are documented; download requires free registration at idd.insaan.iiit.ac.in.
Camera-only dataset (monocular, crowdsourced from taxi vehicles); no LiDAR, radar, or any non-visual sensors; released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for free non-commercial use.
Exclusively a dashcam (monocular) video dataset from DiDi's ride-hailing fleet in China; no sensor modalities beyond the front-facing camera are present or mentioned in the paper or project page.
Dataset (BMVC 2024) uses four RGB cameras (front, front-left, front-right, back), six 77 GHz FMCW radars, one LiDAR, GPS, and IMU; access requires Google Form approval and a data usage agreement.

ROAD re-annotates 22 videos from the Oxford RobotCar Dataset with road-event bounding-box tubes (agent/action/location triplets); only monocular video frames and annotations are distributed — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS data is included in the ROAD release itself.

Image-only dataset crowdsourced from diverse cameras (phones, tablets, action cams); GPS metadata is provided at image level; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or vehicle bus data; download requires a free Mapillary account and agreement to CC BY-NC-SA license.

MSLS is a crowdsourced place-recognition dataset (CVPR 2020) providing 1.6M monocular street-level images with GPS coordinates, UTM coordinates, compass angle, and timestamps; no LiDAR, radar, or IMU are included.
Camera-only lane detection dataset; all 133,235 frames are annotated with lane markings using cubic splines; no additional sensors documented.
Image-only dataset (1280×720 px) of US highway driving; the GitHub README explicitly states no calibration file exists and no non-camera sensors are included.
Image-only lane detection benchmark (150K RGB frames at 2650×1440 px); no additional sensor modalities beyond a single forward-facing camera are documented in the paper or GitHub.

Camera-only lane detection dataset (100 videos, 10,000 frames) captured with a monocular front-facing camera; no LiDAR/radar/IMU/GPS; released under CC BY-NC-SA via Google Drive/Baidu Disk, though at least one survey (arXiv:2504.08540) reports the dataset may no longer be accessible.
LiDAR was used internally to build HD maps for automatic annotation but is not released; only camera images with pixel-level lane annotations are distributed, and an account is required to download.

OpenLane is a camera-image-and-annotation-only 3D lane benchmark built on Waymo Open Dataset; raw LiDAR/IMU/GPS from the underlying Waymo data are not redistributed — only front-camera frames, lane annotations, camera extrinsics/intrinsics, and ego pose are provided; access requires Waymo Open Dataset registration.

OpenLane-V2 is explicitly camera-centric, built on Argoverse 2 (subset_A) and nuScenes (subset_B); its own data format includes only multi-view camera images, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, ego pose, and SD maps — no LiDAR/radar/IMU/GPS are exposed, though source datasets originally contain them. Access requires agreeing to both nuScenes and Argoverse 2 terms of use.

Camera-only (~43k real-world frames at 1920×1208 px, highways and urban scenes); hosted by 42dot under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 requiring license acceptance at https://www.42dot.ai/akit/dataset; no other sensor modalities documented in the CVPR 2022 paper or dataset page.
ELAS (Ego-Lane Analysis System) is a monocular-camera-only lane detection dataset of 20+ real-world scenes (~15,000 frames) recorded in Brazil, with no additional sensor modalities documented.
Camera-only dataset (~20,000 RGB frames at 640×480) collected in Seoul across four weather/lighting scenarios; download requires completing a registration survey on GitHub.
Image-only road marking detection dataset (2887 frames, 11 classes) recorded with two vehicle-mounted cameras in Sri Lanka; no non-visual sensors are present.

GTSRB is a single-image, multi-class traffic sign classification benchmark captured with a Prosilica GC 1380CH monocular camera at 25 fps during real on-road drives in Germany; it contains only cropped sign images with no other sensor modalities.
GTSDB is a purely image-based traffic sign detection benchmark (900 real still images, monocular camera only) with bounding box annotations; no other sensors, ego-motion, or 3D data are included.

BTSC (Belgian Traffic Sign Classification) is a real-world dataset of cropped traffic sign images from 8 cameras (4 stereo pairs) mounted on a recording van; camera poses are included in the full BelgiumTS release, but IMU/GPS are not explicitly documented.

BTSD (BelgiumTS) is a Belgian traffic sign dataset with 8 high-resolution cameras mounted on a van providing video sequences, camera calibrations, and poses; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS data are included.

Camera-only dataset (monocular, varying resolutions, color and grayscale) focused solely on traffic sign detection and recognition; released under an academic license agreement requiring acceptance before download.
Image-only dataset sourced from Tencent Street View panoramas; annotated with bounding boxes and pixel masks for traffic signs under CC BY-NC 2.0; no non-camera sensors present.

Image-only dataset of ~7,000 high-resolution RGB images across 200 traffic sign categories captured on Slovenian roads; no sensor modalities beyond the vehicle-mounted camera are included or documented.

MTSD is a pure image-based traffic sign detection/classification dataset (105K crowd-sourced street-level photos); no depth, LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or vehicle data is included. Access requires a free Mapillary account registration.

CURE-TSR contains ~2.2M traffic sign images cropped from real-world BelgiumTS video sequences and Unreal Engine 4 simulator frames; it is a pure image classification dataset with no additional sensor modalities; download requires registration via a form on the official project page or IEEE DataPort.

Dataset contains ~1.72M video frames split into 49 real-world and 49 synthetic (Unreal Engine 4) sequences with 12 challenging condition types; only monocular camera video is provided — no other sensors documented.

STSD is a monocular-camera-only traffic sign detection/recognition dataset; no additional sensors (LiDAR, GPS, IMU, radar, stereo) are documented anywhere in the official CVL page or any citing paper.

RTSD (Russian Traffic Sign Dataset) is a traffic sign detection/classification dataset captured solely via monocular widescreen dashcam DVRs at 5 fps; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or other sensor modalities are present. Publicly available via Kaggle and Yandex Disk.
Image-only Chinese traffic sign detection benchmark (monocular camera); no sensor modalities beyond 2D images; dataset hosted on Baidu Netdisk and freely accessible via the GitHub repository.

Released dataset contains only RGB monocular images (13,427 frames, 1280×720); the accompanying ICRA 2017 paper describes a system using stereo vision and odometry, but only the RGB modality is publicly released, for non-commercial use only.

Dataset includes stereo camera (left + disparity), a wide-angle (130° HFOV) lens camera, and GPS; paper mentions velocity/yaw rate/radar objects as fusable CAN-bus signals but it is unclear if these are released in the public dataset download.
Camera-only dataset (Marling F-046C monocular, 640×480 RGB at 25 Hz) of 11,179 frames recorded in Paris; no additional sensors are documented on the official project page.
Image-only traffic light detection dataset (5,786 real-world images, 5 classes); no sensor modalities beyond a monocular camera are documented anywhere in the repo or associated SCRDet++ paper.

The Intel Realsense T265 is a stereo fisheye tracking camera; OS1-64 LiDAR and IMU calibration files are explicitly provided; no mention of GPS, radar, CAN bus, or ego-pose trajectory on the official dataset page.
Ego pose (3D camera pose per frame) is derived from Structure-from-Motion calibration sequences, not from GPS/IMU; no other sensor modalities are present beyond the monocular HD camera.

DUS (Daimler Urban Segmentation) is a stereo grayscale camera-only dataset of 5000 rectified image pairs for semantic segmentation in urban traffic; no LiDAR, radar, GPS/IMU, or other sensors are documented.
Fully synthetic dataset; 8 RGB cameras form a binocular 360° rig with depth sensors; GPS and IMU present in SYNTHIA-SF sub-variant; download requires registration at synthia-dataset.net.
Dataset consists exclusively of 24,966 synthetic GTA5 RGB frames with dense pixel-level semantic labels; no sensor modalities beyond a single virtual monocular camera are provided.
Synscapes is a purely synthetic, single-camera (monocular RGB + depth + semantic/instance labels) dataset for street scene parsing; it contains no LiDAR, radar, stereo, or any other sensor modality.

Fully synthetic dataset rendered from GTA V via the DeepGTAV-PreSIL plugin; 50,000+ frames with HD RGB images, precise LiDAR point clouds, depth maps, semantic segmentation, IMU data, and vehicle control variables; no real-world sensors.

Purely synthetic rendered dataset (semi-procedural Unreal Engine scenes); only modality is monocular RGB images with pixel-level ground-truth labels (semantic, instance, depth, 2D boxes); no physical sensors or vehicle telemetry of any kind.

Synthetic CARLA-based dataset with four surround-view monocular cameras and 360° LiDAR; odometry provided; no radar, IMU, GPS, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented; downloadable under a non-commercial license.

Fishyscapes is a camera-only (RGB) benchmark built on Cityscapes imagery; FS Static overlays synthetic objects onto real frames (Mixed), while FS Lost & Found uses real road anomalies; full test sets require evaluation-server submission tied to a Cityscapes account (registration required).
Camera-only image benchmark (RoadAnomaly21 + RoadObstacle21) for anomaly and obstacle segmentation; no raw sensor modalities beyond RGB images are provided.
Dataset is stereo-vision only (left/right images + precomputed disparity); no LiDAR, IMU, GPS, or other sensors; download requires email registration with Daimler researchers.
Both RoadAnomaly21 and RoadObstacle21 are image-only (monocular camera) benchmarks from the SegmentMeIfYouCan suite; no other sensor modalities are present.
MUAD is a vision-only synthetic image dataset (RGB + depth + semantic/instance/object annotations); no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS modalities are included; download requires filling out a Google Form.
Four fisheye surround-view cameras with HD LiDAR, IMU, and GNSS confirmed in paper; CAN bus / vehicle odometry not explicitly documented despite end-to-end driving labels being provided.

SynWoodScape is a purely synthetic surround-view fisheye camera dataset generated in CARLA Simulator with four 190° FOV fisheye cameras and 80k images annotated for 10+ vision tasks (semantic segmentation, depth, optical flow, etc.); no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GNSS data are documented in the released dataset, only camera imagery and derived annotations.

Fully synthetic dataset generated from CARLA and GTA V simulators; provides stereo fisheye and catadioptric omnidirectional images from a motorcycle with semantic segmentation, depth maps, camera intrinsics, and dynamic vehicle parameters (speed, acceleration, pitch/roll/yaw) — no real-world sensor hardware involved.

Dataset contains 10 clips (~7.25 hrs) of highway driving from a windshield-mounted camera on an Acura ILX 2016, with synchronized logs of speed, steering angle, acceleration, gyroscope, and GPS at 100 Hz; released under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
Radar data comes from the car's built-in forward radar captured via CAN/panda, not a standalone sensor; dataset is ~100GB, MIT-licensed, and freely available via Academic Torrents and HuggingFace.
Dataset comprises ROS bags with monocular camera (Point Grey), Velodyne LiDAR, GPS, IMU, and steering/throttle/brake telemetry; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors documented.

Sensors are limited to two monocular cameras (ETG eye-tracking glasses at 720p + roof-mounted GoPro at 1080p), with GPS, car speed, and car course (heading) as the only non-visual metadata; no LiDAR, radar, or IMU are present.

In-cabin driver behavior dataset with 6 synchronized RGB-D views (color, infrared, depth) and 3D body pose; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or vehicle bus data — login requirement was removed and data is now freely accessible for research.

DMD is a driver-facing (in-cabin) monitoring dataset with RGB, Depth, and IR streams from 3 camera perspectives (face, body, hands) recorded in both a real car and a driving simulator; it is not an exterior/road perception dataset and contains no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or vehicle odometry.

Dataset captures in-cabin face camera and forward-facing road camera from real-world driving; GPS/speed signals included; wearable/tactile sensors mentioned on project page but IMU/CAN-bus specifics are not explicitly documented in available sources.

DriveLM-Data is Mixed: DriveLM-nuScenes is real-world (inheriting nuScenes' 6 cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 radars, GPS, IMU, CAN bus, ego pose), while DriveLM-CARLA is synthetic (CARLA simulator); download requires completing a registration form.

Dataset uses only a single front-facing monocular camera; the paper explicitly states LiDAR and other sensors are excluded; access requires agreeing to a non-commercial license on the official GitHub/website.
Dataset explicitly provides LiDAR BEV point clouds and wide-angle panoramic cameras (front, left-rear, right-rear); radar, IMU, GPS, CAN bus are not mentioned in any official documentation.

Reason2Drive is a video-text QA benchmark derived from nuScenes, Waymo, and ONCE; sensor modalities reflect those source datasets (cameras, LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, CAN bus from nuScenes/Waymo/ONCE) rather than newly collected raw sensor data.

Video-only dataset (2059 hrs: 1747 hrs YouTube + 312 hrs public datasets); camera is monocular dashcam footage; all annotations are auto-generated text captions/commands — no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or any non-camera sensor data present or documented.

Dataset contains only RGB images and COLMAP-derived camera poses (5-camera rig, 1920×1080); no LiDAR, radar, IMU, GPS, or CAN bus data are provided; download requires agreeing to a non-commercial research licence.

NAVSIM is a benchmark framework built on OpenScene (a redistribution of nuPlan real-world data); it provides 8 surround cameras, merged LiDAR from 5 sensors, ego status (velocity/acceleration), and ego pose trajectories; GNSS/IMU are part of the underlying nuPlan collection setup; data download requires registration at nuplan.org.

The robot carried a Velodyne HDL-32 LiDAR, Garmin GPS, and Microstrain IMU during collection, but only monocular RGB video frames with pixel-wise semantic annotations are publicly released; no LiDAR, GPS, or IMU data are distributed.

Seven sensing modalities on a Yamaha Viking ATV: stereo+mono RGB cameras, one LiDAR, IMU, GPS, wheel encoders, and suspension/shock travel sensors; TartanDrive 2.0 (arxiv 2402.01913) added three additional LiDARs and confirmed the 1.0 sensor suite.
Thermal camera confirmed by AirLab offroad page; vehicle odometry via Racepak G2X Pro (steering, throttle/brake, RPM); no radar, fisheye, or event camera found in any official source.

GOOSE is a semantic segmentation dataset for unstructured off-road environments recorded on the MuCAR-3 platform; CAN bus/vehicle odometry not explicitly documented, though drive-by-wire dead reckoning is mentioned.

GOOSE-Ex extends the original GOOSE dataset with ~5000 labeled multimodal frames from a Fraunhofer IOSB excavator (ALICE) and quadruped robot (SpotLow); radar/thermal/event camera absence is inferred from no mention in sensor setup descriptions.
Dataset provides only synchronized RGB image and LiDAR point cloud pairs for off-road freespace detection; no IMU, GPS, radar, or ego-pose data are documented.

CaT (CAVS Traversability Dataset) is a real off-road dataset of 12,300 monocular images with IMU-derived roughness labels, hosted publicly at cavs.msstate.edu; no explicit documentation found for LiDAR, radar, GPS, CAN bus, or ego-pose.

YCOR (Yamaha-CMU Off-Road) is an image-only semantic segmentation dataset of 1,076 real RGB frames; the vehicle platform used camera, LiDAR, and IMU for navigation but only labeled RGB images are included in the public release.

Off-road boreal forest robot navigation dataset (not urban autonomous driving); hosted on AWS Open Data Registry; sensors confirmed from paper: 2x LiDAR (RoboSense + Leishen), Navtech FMCW radar, stereo + monocular cameras, 2x IMU, 3x GNSS.

Dataset provides RGB, Depth, NIR, NRG, NDVI, and EVI multi-spectral image modalities for forest semantic segmentation; no LiDAR, radar, IMU, or GPS sensors are included — depth is sensor-derived (likely structured light), and stereo status is undocumented.

Dataset consists solely of real dashcam videos (1584×660, 30 fps) crowd-sourced from public video websites (YouTube, Bilibili, etc.) with eye-tracking fixation annotations collected via a lab-mounted SMI RED250 infrared eye tracker; no vehicle-mounted sensors beyond the monocular camera are included.
DoTA consists solely of 4,677 dashcam (monocular RGB) video clips sourced from YouTube, with temporal/spatial/categorical anomaly annotations; no non-visual sensor modalities are present.
CCD (Car Crash Dataset, ACM MM 2020) is a dashcam-only video dataset of 1,500 accident and 3,000 normal YouTube videos; it contains no additional sensor modalities beyond the monocular camera stream.
DAD (Dashcam Accident Dataset) is a video-only dataset of 1,750 dashcam videos from six cities in Taiwan, introduced at ACCV 2016 for accident anticipation; no non-camera sensors are present.

CADP is a traffic accident detection/forecasting dataset of 1,416 YouTube-sourced CCTV video clips with spatio-temporal annotations; it contains only monocular RGB video — no ego-vehicle sensors of any kind.

Dataset uses two PointGrey color cameras (frontal-facing) and a Velodyne HDL-64ES3 LiDAR; no explicit documentation found for IMU, GPS, CAN bus, or ego pose; data access requires a registration/request process via the GitHub repository.

No paper, project page, or GitHub repository for an autonomous driving dataset named 'ROL' could be found across multiple web searches; the name may be an acronym variant, a very obscure or internal dataset, or a possible typo.
CAP-DATA is a dashcam-only video benchmark (11,727 clips) for accident prediction; later refined and renamed MM-AU; download requires BaiduNetDisk extraction code or HuggingFace registration.

Dataset is video-only (forward monocular dashcam); in-camera IMU is used internally as a recording trigger but no IMU, GPS, or other sensor streams are provided; tabular metadata covers light conditions, weather, scene type, and event timing only.

LiDAR was used only to generate disparity ground-truth labels via a model-guided filtering strategy; raw LiDAR, GPS, IMU, or odometry data are not released — only stereo image pairs, disparity maps, and depth maps are publicly distributed under the MIT license.

Dataset provides six global-shutter monocular cameras (360° coverage) and Luminar-H2 LiDAR only; ego poses are included via the DGP format; no radar, IMU, GPS, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal sensors are documented.

Fully synthetic dataset (FlyingThings3D, Driving, Monkaa) rendered with Blender; provides stereo RGB frames plus dense ground-truth optical flow, disparity, disparity change, and segmentation — no real-world sensors of any kind.

Fully synthetic dataset extracted from GTA V; all sensor data is virtual — ground-truth ego pose and visual odometry are provided as game-engine outputs, not from physical sensors.
SIM10K is a purely image-based synthetic dataset (RGB frames from GTA5) with 2D bounding-box annotations for cars only; no other sensor modalities are included.

Synthetic CARLA-simulator dataset for odometry/SLAM tasks; sensors explicitly listed in paper Table 1 as 2 LiDARs (16-ch and 64-ch), 1 monocular camera, GPS, and IMU; no radar, stereo, fisheye, event, or thermal cameras documented.

MetaDrive is a driving simulator (not a static dataset); it generates synthetic scenarios procedurally and can also replay real-world logs from Waymo/nuScenes/Argoverse — sensors are simulated (ray-cast LiDAR, RGB/Depth/Semantic cameras); no stereo, fisheye, event, thermal, radar, IMU, or GPS sensors are documented.

ScenarioNet is not a raw sensor dataset but an open-source platform (NeurIPS 2023) that converts real-world logs (Waymo, nuScenes, nuPlan, Lyft L5, Argoverse) and synthetic scenarios into a unified internal scenario description storing HD maps and agent trajectories — raw sensor modalities (camera, lidar, radar, IMU, GPS) are not included in its internal format.

Fully synthetic dataset collected inside CARLA simulator (v2) by the Think2Drive RL expert; 6 surround monocular RGB cameras, 1 LiDAR, 5 radars, plus IMU/GPS/control signals all from CARLA API; released on HuggingFace under CC-BY-NC-ND license.

Fully synthetic dataset generated via simulator; sensor suite explicitly lists 8 modalities (RGB, Stereo, Depth, LiDAR, SPAD-LiDAR, Radar, IMU, GPS); CAN bus/odometry and ego-pose trajectory streams are not explicitly documented.

LimSim++ is a synthetic closed-loop simulation platform (not a sensor dataset) for deploying Multimodal LLMs in autonomous driving; it provides structured scene/traffic state information to LLMs rather than raw physical sensor data, and is open-source on GitHub (PJLab-ADG/LimSim, branch LimSim_plus).

SUMMIT is a CARLA-based open-source simulator (not a static dataset) for dense unregulated urban traffic using real-world OSM maps; sensor availability inherits from CARLA's sensor suite as documented in the ICRA 2020 paper and GitHub/docs pages.

LUMPI is a fixed infrastructure/roadside dataset (not ego-vehicle); sensors are explicitly documented as up to 3 RGB cameras and up to 5 LiDARs — no radar, IMU, GPS, or ego-motion data is present.

Static MLS+ALS LiDAR point-cloud dataset (Han et al. ISPRS JPRS 2024 209:500-513); released H5 files contain only points/semantic+instance labels/intensity/number-of-returns — panoramic images mentioned in abstract are not in standard download.
